final.investment_thesis:
All three seats and the trader independently landed on the same executable — keep_shares at 1.49% — so the decision is not the transaction, it is which conditional framework governs the next move. I weigh it as follows.

The bull wins the business-quality question decisively and nobody rebutted it. Nine-month FY2026 diluted EPS of $6.88 (+22.4%) on revenue +16.1%, gross margin 49.07% (+225 bp) with Q3 at 50.06% (+357 bp), gross-profit growth accelerating 18.8% → 22.1% → 25.3% across three quarters, net cash up 84% to $62.22B with zero new long-term debt issuance, receivables down 21.1% against revenue up 16.1%, and $117.0B of nine-month operating cash flow. Price sits roughly 10% above a rising 200-SMA at 281.70 (up from 253.92 since April) with a +10.2% 50/200 golden-cross spread. The bear conceded the earnings are real; that concession removes the 'broken franchise' case and is why the rating is not Underweight or Sell. The Jefferies $263.66 target is a single truncated re-report of a 10 August note built on a September 2027 event — at roughly 30x trailing EPS it is a multiple opinion, not an earnings forecast.

The bear wins the entry-asymmetry question, and it wins on arithmetic rather than narrative. The conservative seat's exchange is the decisive one in the debate: enter at the trader's 316.83 trigger with the structural 300.00 stop and risk is 16.83 a share, so 320.04 pays 0.19:1, the 329.59 gap bottom pays 0.76:1, and only the 333.43 gap top reaches 0.99:1 — you need a new all-time high at 340.08 to get 1.38:1. The aggressive seat's 'better than four to one' is only reachable by mixing an entry at 310.34 with a reward to the gap fill and a stop 5.3% below a 316.83 fill; those three numbers cannot come from two different prices. The neutral seat said the same thing more cleanly and I adopt it. The tape corroborates: 310.34 is below the 50-SMA (310.50), below the Bollinger basis (313.01), MACD is −1.488 below zero and below signal, VWMA at 309.15 puts the volume-weighted buyer at breakeven, the highs descend 319.28 → 320.28 → 313.36, the 08-20 rejection at 320.28 lands on the exact 50% retrace of the 07-31 gap, and volume has collapsed to 34.7M from 132.5M on the distribution day.

The aggressive seat loses on two specific points. First, volume/volatility compression is direction-agnostic — the neutral is right that a histogram contracting 93.5% from −3.634 to −0.235 while MACD stays below zero and below signal is the definition of a decline stopping, not an advance starting; he is not reading the coil, he is betting on it. Second, he converts 'the position is tiny, so risk is trivial' (correct: 4.7968 shares to 300.00 is ~$49.60, five basis points of equity) into an argument to make the position bigger, which is a direction preference wearing a risk analysis. The conservative's inversion is the right one: a small position cannot hurt you, and the evidence is explicitly unresolved.

The conservative seat wins the arithmetic but loses the conditional design, and the neutral seat is the best arbitration. Requiring a close above 320.28 plus >60M volume plus MACD back above zero plus an ideal retest demands a completed trend repair, which buys the trade at the price where the 329.59–333.43 gap supply is already overhead. His 302.94 exit sits inside the 300.00–302.94 band that has absorbed four tests (08-03, 08-04, 08-12, 08-17) with no close beneath it — the same noise problem he correctly criticized in the 302.1 ATR stop, since ATR at 7.37 means a single 2.4% session takes you from 310 to 303 with no information conveyed. And the 2.0% versus 3.0% cap is roughly fifty dollars of risk difference on a position he opened by conceding is too small to matter. The neutral's 319.28 trigger (the 08-19 high, clearing the bounce structure without front-running the 320.28 rejection) on >55M shares with the histogram flipping positive, staged half-on-confirmation, half-on-hold, with the structural 300.00 stop and the trader's 300.57-with-expanding-volume exit, is the construct I authorize. I also prefer the neutral's two-sided read of inventory: raw materials +260% with finished goods −4% is a pre-buy ahead of a ramp, which is simultaneously the component-shortage risk and the hedge against it, not the one-sided bear signal the conservative presents.

What keeps this a Hold rather than Underweight is threefold. The bear's core mechanism is multiple compression (35.5x toward 29x), which is a slow, catalyst-light process, not a reason to act on one week's tape — the bear effectively conceded no fundamental deterioration is required, which is a valuation statement, not a next-quarter forecast. There is no downside confirmation: no close below 300.57 in 17 sessions and RSI 48.23 offers no oversold edge in either direction. And practically, the marginal risk on 1.49% is ~5 bp of equity, so paying 10 bps to move it is a negative-expectancy trade. Prior AAPL outcomes reinforce exactly this: the 08-13, 08-12, 08-11 and 08-17 Underweights each bled alpha by trimming into support above a rising 200-SMA, and the standing lesson from those reflections is to require a confirmed daily close below the floor rather than act on volume decay. The 08-20 add at 2.5% and 08-24 cut to 1.5% — $1.89 of fees to end up three shares smaller — is the concrete warning against a third round trip in five sessions; note price risk has cost this account $390.57 realized against $46.31 of cumulative fees.

What would change the call. Upgrade toward Overweight: a daily close above 319.28 on >55M shares with the MACD histogram turning positive — staged to 3.0% of equity (~$2,990, ~9.6 shares) at the next open, stop structural at 300.00, second half only on a hold of the reclaimed level; a volume-backed fill of the 329.59–333.43 gap would extend toward 340.08. Downgrade toward Sell: a daily close below 300.57, ideally below 300.00, on expanding volume — rebalance to 0.00% and do not average down. Between 300.57 and 319.28, including the entire 305–311 band the bull proposed, hold at 1.49% and let the coil resolve. Diligence gaps stated plainly rather than inferred: the $13.27B gross intangibles step-up and $13.53B (+32.6%) other-noncurrent-liability increase have no 8-K or footnote in the dataset and must be resolved before any size increase; there is no FY2026 Q4 company guidance anywhere in the evidence; insider and sentiment data are unavailable; and 85 of 105 news records were not supplied, including nothing explaining the 07-31 −7.35% gap. Opex +21.9% and R&D +32.5% against revenue +16.1% mean every basis point of FY2026 margin expansion is gross margin doing the work, and the documented 1–2 quarter input-cost pass-through lag means Q3's 50.06% predates the escalation — that is the burden of proof the bull has not yet discharged. Deferred revenue +8.8% against revenue +16.1% is a negative mix tell for the Services engine, tax rate +219 bp (Q3 at 17.86% vs 16.40%) is an unmentioned EPS headwind, and roughly $10.8B of the FCF strength is a non-repeating cash-tax timing benefit. Finally, the week carries two-sided exogenous risk — NVDA earnings and Jackson Hole — that cannot be handicapped in either direction; the correct response to unhandicappable event risk is position size, and 1.49% is already the smallest this account has held.
